questions.text: Tell me about the work you do or the subject you study.
questions.say: Good afternoon. My name is George, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about work or studies. Tell me about the work you do or the subject you study.

questions.text: What do you enjoy most about your work or your studies?
questions.say: What do you enjoy most about your work or your studies?

questions.text: Is there anything you find difficult about it?

questions.text: What would you like to do in the next few years?

questions.text: What kind of weather do you like best?
questions.say: Now let's move on to talk about the weather. What kind of weather do you like best?

questions.text: Does the weather ever change your plans?
questions.say: Does the weather ever change your plans?

questions.text: Is the weather where you live different now from when you were a child?

questions.say: Now let's move on to talk about reading. Do you read much in your free time?

cueCard.topic: Describe a book you have read that you found interesting.
cueCard.explain: and explain why you found it interesting.

questions.text: Describe a book you have read that you found interesting.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a book you have read that you found interesting. You should say: what the book was; when you read it; what it was about; and explain why you found it interesting.

questions.text: Would you recommend this book to your friends?
questions.say: Thank you. Would you recommend this book to your friends?

questions.text: Why do you think some people read a lot and others hardly read at all?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a book you found interesting, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all reading habits. Why do you think some people read a lot and others hardly read at all?

questions.text: Do you think children read less now than in the past? Why?
questions.say: Do you think children read less now than in the past? Why?

questions.text: How can parents encourage their children to read more?
questions.say: How can parents encourage their children to read more?

questions.text: Do you think printed books will disappear in the future?
questions.say: Now let's talk about books and technology. Do you think printed books will disappear in the future?

questions.text: What are the advantages of reading on a screen?
questions.say: What are the advantages of reading on a screen?

questions.text: Should public libraries still be funded by governments today?
